baskets.weighting_caveat: First-pass revenue-share weights, normalized over the four TrendForce-named public operators (their raw 33.7/17.3/17.1/13.9 of a 100% market summing to 82% public coverage). Explicitly revisable in v2. The remaining ~18% (SK Siltron CSS captive/private, Resonac, STMicro, smaller Chinese names) is not in the basket, so the basket over-represents these four relative to true global supply. The Wolfspeed Chapter 11 reset means pre-Sept-2025 WOLF price history must be treated as a separate, terminated series; do NOT splice old and new WOLF closes when computing the proxy.

constituents.name: Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd.
constituents.source: Industry consensus (multiple market reports, e.g. Mordor Intelligence, QYResearch/openPR freestanding-GaN studies 2024) identify Sumitomo Electric as the dominant freestanding/bulk-GaN substrate supplier via its proprietary low-dislocation HVPE process. Top-3 (Sumitomo Electric + SCIOCS + Mitsubishi Chemical) = 78.84% of the 2024 freestanding-GaN market (QYResearch via openPR). No clean public per-company split exists; Sumitomo Electric assigned the largest of the three as the recognized leader (qualitative/estimated, NOT a published precise figure).
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Widely regarded as the #1 freestanding GaN substrate producer, but NO published precise single-company percentage exists - weight is a qualitative estimate within the 78.84% top-3 cluster (hence reduced basket confidence). NEGLIGIBLE exposure purity: Sumitomo Electric is a ~JPY 4-trillion-revenue conglomerate (automotive wiring harnesses, electric wire/cable, optical fiber, infocomm); bulk GaN substrate is a rounding-error revenue line. The stock will essentially not track GaN substrate ASPs.

constituents.name: Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd. (SCIOCS Company)
constituents.source: QYResearch/openPR freestanding-GaN 2024: SCIOCS named in the top-3 (combined 78.84%). SCIOCS Company Ltd. is a Sumitomo Chemical subsidiary (formerly Hitachi Cable's GaN business). Per-company share is estimated, not published; assigned the middle of the three.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: SCIOCS is a recognized top-3 freestanding-GaN and GaN-epi supplier, but its share is bundled in the 78.84% top-3 figure with no clean split (estimated weight). NEGLIGIBLE purity: SCIOCS is a small subsidiary of Sumitomo Chemical (4005.T), a multi-segment chemicals giant (petrochemicals, agro, pharma, IT-related materials). GaN is immaterial to the parent's equity. NOTE: ticker 4005.T is Sumitomo Chemical; some sources list Sumitomo Chemical as 4005.T on TSE.

constituents.name: Mitsubishi Chemical Group Corp.
constituents.source: QYResearch/openPR freestanding-GaN 2024: Mitsubishi Chemical named in the top-3 (combined 78.84%). Per-company share is estimated, not published; assigned the smallest of the three.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Mitsubishi Chemical runs an ammonothermal bulk-GaN effort and is a recognized top-3 supplier, but its GaN substrate operation is effectively a small/semi-carved-out unit and its share within the 78.84% top-3 is not separately published (estimated weight). NEGLIGIBLE purity: parent Mitsubishi Chemical Group (4188.T) is one of the world's largest diversified chemical companies; GaN substrate is immaterial to the equity.

excluded_private: Mitsubishi Chemical's bulk-GaN operation is sometimes described as a quasi-private/internal unit - its standalone economics are not separately disclosed even though the parent (4188.T) is public
Suzhou Nanowin (Sino Nitride) - private Chinese freestanding-GaN entrant scaling 2-4 inch capacity
Eta Research Ltd. - private Chinese GaN substrate entrant

Soitec (SOI.PA) and Sumco (3436.T) make GaN-on-Si / engineered-substrate epi, NOT bulk freestanding GaN - excluded from the freestanding-substrate basket (different product; both also low/negligible GaN purity)
Sumitomo Electric's, SCIOCS's and Mitsubishi's exact individual shares are themselves effectively undisclosed (private within the conglomerates)
baskets.confidence_rationale: Although public parent companies cover ~79% of the freestanding-GaN market (top-3 = 78.84%, all three parents listed), this basket is LOW confidence for three compounding reasons: (1) EVERY constituent is negligible-purity - Sumitomo Electric, Sumitomo Chemical and Mitsubishi Chemical are giant diversified conglomerates where bulk GaN is a rounding-error revenue line, so none of the stocks will meaningfully track GaN substrate ASPs; (2) there is NO published per-company share split inside the 78.84% top-3 cluster, so the intra-basket weights are qualitative estimates, not defensible market-share figures (per anti-fabrication rules this forces lower confidence); and (3) the bulk freestanding-GaN market is tiny (~$400M in 2024), so even the leaders capture immaterial revenue. The proxy is directionally informative about WHO supplies GaN substrates but is a weak price-discovery instrument.
baskets.weighting_caveat: First-pass weights are QUALITATIVE ESTIMATES (Sumitomo Electric > SCIOCS > Mitsubishi within the 78.84% top-3) because no public per-company freestanding-GaN share is disclosed - these are explicitly NOT defensible precise percentages and are flagged for v2 revision. Because all three constituents are negligible-purity diversified conglomerates, the basket will track the broad Japanese chemical/industrial equity complex far more than GaN substrate prices. Sumitomo Chemical ticker shown as 4005.T (parent of SCIOCS); confirm exact TSE code in implementation.

constituents.name: Wacker Chemie AG
constituents.source: Wacker 2024 Annual Report (Polysilicon segment) + Wacker corporate statements: Wacker is the self-described and industry-recognized global market LEADER in hyperpure semiconductor-grade polysilicon; the hyperpure semi-grade share of its volumes rose again in 2024 and it aims to double semiconductor sales by 2030. Search syntheses citing Wacker+Hemlock at ~3/4 of the semi-poly market. Public semi-grade-specific percentages are not disclosed; weight is an estimate reflecting clear #1 status among PUBLIC producers (Hemlock, the other co-leader, is private).
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Recognized global #1 in electronic/semiconductor-grade (11N) polysilicon. Largest PUBLIC pure exposure to semi-grade poly. MEDIUM purity: Wacker's Polysilicon division is one of several divisions (Silicones, Polymers, Biosolutions also large), and even within Polysilicon the SOLAR-grade business has historically dominated volume/revenue (2024 Polysilicon sales fell 40.6% to EUR 949m mostly on solar weakness). So the equity carries large non-semi-poly exposure, but semi-grade is a growing, high-margin, strategically emphasized slice - the best public tracker available.

constituents.name: Tokuyama Corporation
constituents.source: Industry consensus (multiple trade sources): Tokuyama is widely described as the world's THIRD-largest semiconductor-grade polysilicon producer (after Wacker and the private Hemlock). Semi-grade-specific share not publicly quantified; weight estimated as clear #2 among public producers.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: World's ~#3 semiconductor-grade polysilicon producer; completed a JPY 30bn Shunan expansion for sub-3nm-node purity in 2024 and is building an OCI JV (OSTM) in Malaysia (commercial ~2029). MEDIUM purity: Tokuyama is a diversified chemicals company (electronic materials, cement, plastics, health care), but electronic-materials/semi-poly is a more material and strategically central slice than at the GaN conglomerates.

constituents.name: GCL Technology Holdings Ltd.
constituents.source: GCL corporate disclosures (gcl-power.com): electronic-grade high-purity (11N, 99.99999999999%) polysilicon capacity of 5,000 t/yr Xuzhou + 10,000 t/yr Inner Mongolia (with TCL JV); claims >50% DOMESTIC (China) electronic-grade share. Global semi-grade share is small and not cleanly disclosed; weight estimated as the smallest public constituent.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Emerging Chinese electronic-grade producer (>50% domestic China share per company), but globally still small versus Wacker/Hemlock/Tokuyama and ramping. LOW purity: GCL is overwhelmingly a SOLAR-grade polysilicon and granular-silicon company (60,000+ t solar capacity in Xuzhou alone); semiconductor-grade is a small, new segment. The equity tracks the (oversupplied, China-priced) SOLAR poly cycle, which the methodology explicitly warns is MISLEADING for semi-grade.

excluded_private: Hemlock Semiconductor Corp. (USA) - PRIVATE (Corning/DuPont JV); the #2 global semiconductor-grade poly producer and co-leader with Wacker. This is the single largest coverage gap - a top-2 producer entirely absent from any public basket.

OCI Holdings semiconductor-grade ambitions sit partly in the private OCI/Tokuyama Malaysia JV (OSTM, ~2029); OCI Holdings (010060.KS) is itself listed but its semi-grade poly is pre-commercial and immaterial today
Mitsubishi Materials / smaller Japanese producers with minor semi-grade output
Solar-grade Chinese majors (Daqo, Tongwei, Xinte) - not semi-grade producers; excluded by design
baskets.confidence_rationale: Held to LOW (despite Wacker being a genuinely strong leader) primarily because of a large PRIVATE coverage gap and weak purity: (1) Hemlock - the co-#1/#2 semiconductor-grade producer globally - is entirely private (Corning/DuPont), so any public basket structurally misses a top-2 supplier; (2) no operator discloses a semi-grade-SPECIFIC market share, so all weights are estimates of relative public-producer rank, not defensible percentages; and (3) purity is compromised because the methodology's own warning bites hard here - Wacker, Tokuyama and especially GCL all carry large SOLAR-grade and/or unrelated-chemicals revenue, and solar-grade poly pricing (currently depressed by Chinese oversupply) moves these stocks in a direction that is explicitly misleading for the 10-20x-priced semi-grade product sold under LTAs. Wacker is the best available single proxy, but the basket as a whole is a soft tracker.
baskets.weighting_caveat: First-pass weights are ESTIMATES of relative standing among PUBLIC semi-grade producers (Wacker #1 > Tokuyama #3-public > GCL emerging), because semiconductor-grade-specific shares are not publicly quantified - explicitly revisable in v2. The basket covers only the public producers and entirely omits Hemlock (private top-2), so it materially under-represents true global semi-grade supply. Because semi-grade prices are set in confidential long-term agreements at a large multiple of the visible solar-grade price, NONE of these equities is a tight price proxy; treat the basket as an indicative supply-side composite rather than a price feed.

constituents.name: AMG Critical Materials N.V.
constituents.source: AMG Critical Materials 2024 Annual Report (published 12 Mar 2025); AMG runs the Mibra mine (Minas Gerais, Brazil) producing tantalum (Ta2O5) concentrate alongside lithium/spodumene, and is repeatedly named in tantalum market-share studies (Mordor, NextMSC) among the top vertically integrated suppliers (top-4 processors Taniobis/Mitsui/AMG/GAM control >50% of output). No clean public Ta-specific percentage exists; weight reflects AMG being the most prominent PUBLIC tantalum-exposed name (estimated/qualitative).
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: AMG is the principal LISTED tantalum-exposed operator (Mibra Ta2O5 concentrate, originally a world-leading tantalum mine). It is one of the named top-tier suppliers but a precise Ta market share is not publicly disclosed (estimated weight). LOW exposure purity: AMG has repositioned around LITHIUM, vanadium and other critical materials; Mibra now centers on a 130 ktpy spodumene/lithium plant using tantalum tailings as feedstock, so tantalum is a minor and shrinking revenue line. The equity tracks lithium/vanadium far more than tantalum.

constituents.name: Pilbara Minerals Ltd.
constituents.source: USGS / INN tantalum coverage: Australian hard-rock lithium operations (Pilgangoora) produce a tantalite (Ta2O5) BY-PRODUCT; Australia is a leading source of tantalum mine supply (USGS import-source data showed Australia ~54% of US Ta concentrate imports 2019-22). No published Pilbara Ta market-share %; weight estimated and small.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Produces tantalite strictly as a BY-PRODUCT of spodumene/lithium mining at Pilgangoora; a real but small contributor to ex-Africa tantalum mine supply. NEGLIGIBLE purity: Pilbara is a pure LITHIUM equity - tantalum is an immaterial by-product credit. Included only to add some non-Central-African mine-supply representation; it will not track tantalum prices.

constituents.name: Mitsui Mining & Smelting Co. (Mitsui Kinzoku)
constituents.source: Tantalum market-share syntheses (Mordor/NextMSC) name Mitsui Kinzoku among the top-4 tantalum processors (Taniobis, Mitsui Kinzoku, AMG, GAM control >50% of output). Mitsui Kinzoku is listed in Tokyo (5706.T). No clean public Ta-specific percentage; weight estimated and small.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: A named top-4 tantalum processor, providing some PUBLIC exposure to the refining/powder stage. NEGLIGIBLE purity: Mitsui Mining & Smelting is a large diversified non-ferrous metals and materials group (zinc, copper, battery materials, electronic materials, auto parts catalysts); tantalum processing is a minor line. Will not track tantalum prices.

excluded_private: Global Advanced Metals Pty Ltd (GAM) - PRIVATE; the leading tantalum producer/processor (~19.4% of tantalum-pentoxide-powder output per NextMSC) and conflict-free/recycling leader. Largest single coverage gap.
Taniobis GmbH (formerly H.C. Starck Tantalum & Niobium; JX/private ownership) - a top-4 tantalum powder processor, private.
Ningxia Orient Tantalum Industry / CNMC Ningxia Orient - state-owned (China), dominant Asian refiner and capacitor-grade powder producer, not investable.
Cabot Corp tantalum legacy (now within GAM lineage); various DRC/Rwanda artisanal coltan miners (~50% of mine supply, informal/private).
Minsur / Mineracao Taboca (Brazil) - tin-niobium-tantalum byproduct, parent Minsur is Peru-listed but Ta is immaterial.
baskets.confidence_rationale: LOW confidence: tantalum has NO clean public pure-play and the largest producers are private or state-owned. The dominant processor (Global Advanced Metals, ~19% of pentoxide powder) is private; the leading refiners Taniobis and Ningxia Orient are private/state; and ~50% of MINE supply is informal DRC/Rwanda coltan. The investable names are all low- or negligible-purity: AMG has pivoted to lithium (tantalum is a minor, shrinking segment at Mibra), Pilbara's tantalite is a pure lithium-mining by-product, and Mitsui Kinzoku's Ta processing is a rounding error in a diversified base-metals group. There is also NO published company-level tantalum market-share table, so the weights are qualitative. The basket captures only a minority slice of a private/state-dominated chain via stocks that overwhelmingly reflect other commodities (mostly lithium).
baskets.weighting_caveat: First-pass weights are QUALITATIVE (AMG as the principal public Ta-exposed name > Pilbara by-product mine supply > Mitsui processing), since no public company-level tantalum market-share figures exist - explicitly revisable in v2 and among the weakest in the set. The basket omits the true tantalum leaders (GAM, Taniobis, Ningxia Orient, DRC/Rwanda artisanal supply), so it under-represents the commodity by a wide margin, and every constituent is dominated by non-tantalum (largely lithium) businesses. Treat as an indicative, low-fidelity proxy only.

constituents.name: CMOC Group Ltd. (China Molybdenum)
constituents.source: CMOC 2024 Annual Results (en.cmoc.com): CMOC Brasil produced 10,024 mt of niobium in 2024 (record), and is the world's SECOND-LARGEST niobium producer (~11% global share per Intel Market Research / multiple syntheses; CBMM ~77-80%). CMOC acquired the Brazil niobium/phosphate business from Anglo American in 2016. Among PUBLIC, directly-investable niobium PRODUCERS, CMOC is essentially the only one with a real production share; weight reflects that.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: World's #2 niobium producer at ~11% global share (CBMM at ~77-80% is private). The ONLY public company that actually MINES and sells niobium at scale. NEGLIGIBLE exposure purity: CMOC is a global copper-cobalt giant (huge DRC copper/cobalt operations, plus molybdenum/tungsten); 2024 net profit was ~RMB 13.5bn driven by copper/cobalt. Niobium is a tiny revenue/earnings line, so the stock tracks copper/cobalt, NOT niobium prices.

constituents.name: Nippon Steel Corp.
constituents.source: Verified holding (CBMM consortium): in 2011 a Japanese-Korean consortium (JFE Steel, Nippon Steel, POSCO, ex-NSSMC) acquired ~15% of CBMM; CBMM controls ~77-80% of global niobium (USGS 2024; PRNewswire historic 84%). Nippon Steel (5401.T) is a consortium member. This is an EQUITY-STAKE exposure, not production; weight is a small token reflecting the passive minority CBMM interest.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Holds a passive minority share of CBMM (the ~80% global niobium leader) via the 2011 ~15% Japanese-Korean consortium. NEGLIGIBLE purity: Nippon Steel is one of the world's largest STEELMAKERS; a passive fractional stake in CBMM is immaterial to its equity, which tracks steel spreads. Included only to represent indirect public exposure to the otherwise-private CBMM.

constituents.name: POSCO Holdings Inc.
constituents.source: Verified holding (CBMM consortium): POSCO is a member of the 2011 ~15% Japanese-Korean consortium owning a stake in CBMM (~80% global niobium share). POSCO Holdings trades on KRX (005490.KS). Equity-stake exposure, not production; small token weight.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Passive minority CBMM stake via the 2011 consortium. NEGLIGIBLE purity: POSCO Holdings is a giant steel-and-battery-materials group; the CBMM interest is immaterial. Indirect, non-tracking exposure to private CBMM.

constituents.name: ITOCHU Corp.
constituents.source: Per Robotnik task brief / consortium structure, ITOCHU (8001.T, Tokyo) is associated with the CBMM stakeholder consortium. Equity/offtake-stake exposure, not production; smallest token weight. (Consortium membership for the trading houses is less precisely documented than the steelmakers' 2011 15% deal, hence the smaller, lower-confidence weight.)
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Trading-house exposure linked to the CBMM consortium / niobium offtake. NEGLIGIBLE purity: ITOCHU is a vast general trading house (energy, food, textiles, machinery, etc.); any niobium-linked interest is immaterial. Indirect, non-tracking.

constituents.name: CITIC Ltd.
constituents.source: Verified holding (CBMM consortium): in 2011 a Chinese consortium led by CITIC (with Anshan, Shougang, Taiyuan, Baosteel) acquired ~15% of CBMM. CITIC Limited trades on HKEX (0267.HK). Equity-stake exposure, not production; small token weight. NOTE: the listed consortium parent is CITIC Limited (0267.HK), not CITIC Resources or CITIC Securities.
constituents.commodity_market_share_note: Passive minority CBMM stake via the 2011 Chinese ~15% consortium. NEGLIGIBLE purity: CITIC Limited is a sprawling conglomerate (financial services, resources, manufacturing, real estate); the CBMM interest is immaterial. Indirect, non-tracking exposure to private CBMM.

excluded_private: CBMM (Companhia Brasileira de Metalurgia e Mineracao, Brazil) - PRIVATE; controls ~77-80% of global niobium (USGS 2024). The overwhelming majority of the commodity is therefore NOT directly investable; only a ~30% equity stake (two 2011 ~15% consortia) is held by listed companies, and even that is immaterial to each holder.
Niobec (Saint-Honore, Quebec) - owned by Magris Resources, PRIVATE; the main non-Brazilian primary niobium (ferroniobium) producer.

Mineracao Taboca / CMOC's own Brazilian unit details are inside CMOC; Anshan, Shougang, Taiyuan, Baosteel (CITIC consortium co-members) are largely state-owned/separately listed steel entities with the same negligible-purity issue.
baskets.confidence_rationale: LOW confidence: niobium is structurally the hardest of the five to proxy publicly because ~77-80% of global supply is CBMM, which is PRIVATE. The only listed company that actually produces niobium at scale is CMOC (~11% share), and for CMOC niobium is a negligible earnings line inside a copper-cobalt major - so even the best constituent does not track niobium prices. The remaining public exposure is purely passive minority equity stakes in CBMM (the ~30% held across the 2011 Japanese-Korean and Chinese consortia), spread across steelmakers and trading houses for whom the stake is immaterial - these are indirect, non-tracking, and their weights are necessarily tiny qualitative tokens. With ~88% of the commodity (CBMM + private Niobec) outside any tracking equity and every constituent negligible-purity, this basket is an ownership map of niobium, not a price proxy.
baskets.weighting_caveat: First-pass weights are QUALITATIVE TOKENS: CMOC gets the majority weight as the only real public producer, and the five consortium members get small tokens reflecting passive ~15%+15% CBMM equity stakes (steelmakers slightly above trading houses; the trading-house/ITOCHU linkage is the least precisely documented). These are NOT defensible market-share percentages and are explicitly flagged for v2 revision. Because CBMM (~80%) and Niobec are private, the basket cannot represent the commodity's price - it should be read as indirect/ownership exposure only, and CMOC's price will be driven by copper and cobalt, not niobium.
